chunks: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Why do you see those whom God, Mighty and Majestic, has dispatched for wretchedness upon the people of misguidance from the armies of the Satans and their consorts to be more numerous than what you see of the Caliph of God whom He dispatched for justice and righteousness from among the Angels? It was said: O Abu Ja'far, how can anything be more numerous than the Angels? He said: As God, Mighty and Majestic, has willed.

The questioner said: O Abu Ja'far, if I were to narrate this hadith to some of the Shi'a, they would deny it. He said: How would they deny it? He said: They would say that the Angels are more numerous than the Satans. He said: You are right. Understand from me what I am saying: there is not a single day or night except that all the Jinn and Satans visit the imams of misguidance, and an equal number of Angels visits the Imam of Guidance — until when the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) comes, Angels descend during it to the Master of the Command in a number that God, Mighty and Majestic, has created — or said: destined — from among the Satans as their equal number.

Then they visit the master of misguidance and bring him fabrications and lies, until perhaps he wakes up in the morning saying: I saw such-and-such. But if one were to ask the Master of the Command about that, he would say: You saw a Satan who informed you of such-and-such, until he would interpret it for him and make known to him the misguidance upon which he stands.

And by God, whoever believes in the Night of Power knows that it belongs to us exclusively, by virtue of the saying of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) to Ali (peace be upon him) when death drew near him: This is your guardian after me — if you obey him you will be rightly guided. But whoever does not believe in what is in the Night of Power is a denier, and whoever believes in the Night of Power while holding a view other than ours — it is not permissible for him in truth except to say that it belongs to us; and whoever does not say so is a liar.

Surely God, Mighty and Majestic, is too exalted to send down the Command with the Spirit and the Angels to a disbeliever, a transgressor. If they say that it descends to the Caliph who claims that authority, then their saying is worthless; and if they say that it does not descend to anyone, it cannot be that something descends upon nothing; and if they say — and they will say — that this is nothing, then they have gone astray with a far-reaching straying.

key_terms.أَئِمَّةُ الضَّلَالَةِ: Imams of misguidance — false leaders who usurped authority
key_terms.أَجْنَادُ الشَّيَاطِينِ: Armies of the Satans — spiritual forces of evil that support false leaders
key_terms.خَلِيفَةُ اللَّهِ: Caliph/Vicegerent of God — the true Imam appointed by God
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Power/Predetermination (Laylat al-Qadr) — the blessed night in Ramadan described in Surah 97, when divine decrees are determined
key_terms.وَلِيُّ الْأَمْرِ: Master/Guardian of the Command — the legitimate Imam of the Ahlulbayt

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about Laylat al-Qadr and the Imamate?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) explains in a detailed discourse that Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Power from Surah 97) belongs exclusively to the Imams of the Ahlulbayt. He clarifies an apparent paradox: while Angels are greater in number than Satans overall, on every day and night the Satans visit the imams of misguidance while an equal number of Angels visits the Imam of Guidance. On Laylat al-Qadr specifically, the Angels descend to the Master of the Command (the Imam), while an equal number of Satans visit the false claimants, bringing them fabrications. This teaching was addressed to a questioner in the early Abbasid period when the question of legitimate religious and political authority was acutely contested.
